title: SM64DS Co-op 0.5.7 preview: seven-player rooms, synchronized combat and color presets

tests: Two local clients: damage, death, respawn and animation synchronization
Online game timing at approximately 30 game ticks per second
Embedded transparent logo and straight-alpha menu compositing
Native UI, chat, three input bindings and fullscreen checks
ROM extraction with Restricted inherited PowerShell policy and a folder containing spaces
Portable frontend checks on Windows, Linux and macOS; Windows 32-bit host integration
Public archive privacy and hash validation

notes:
Seven-player Windows preview with separate lobbies, automatic server discovery, usernames, head labels, chat, host/moderator commands, three keyboard/controller bindings per action and widescreen fullscreen.

This update synchronizes player-owned damage, health, death, respawn and animations; avoids a redundant online frame wait; adds RGB sliders, grouped overalls/pants, saved presets and CoopDX .ini import/export; improves menu text and embeds the supplied logo with transparency. The bundled ROM extractor now sets PowerShell policy only for its own process.

**How to play**
1. Extract the Windows ZIP. Existing users replace the EXE and server profile after quitting, keeping their ROM, saves, settings and extracted assets.
2. Put your own supported .nds beside the EXE if assets have not been extracted. Open sm64ds coop.exe.
3. Choose HOST ONLINE to create a room and share its room code. Friends choose JOIN ONLINE and enter that code. No IP or port entry is required. Every player needs this version (protocol 5).
4. OPTIONS -> PLAYER -> CHARACTER COLORS opens the sliders. COLOR PRESETS includes Save, Apply, Import CoopDX .INI and Export.

The server operator must keep WGS and the outbound tunnel running. The client profile contains the public Playit address and a public discovery key; it contains no home IP or private agent credential. The ZIP includes no ROM or extracted game assets.

Combat and timing were retested with two local clients; this is not a seven-PC internet performance certification. Linux/SteamOS and macOS playable ports are the next priorities. Android and iOS follow later. Current cross-platform CI checks components, not complete native game builds.
